I will keep the same wheat-maize rotation on all 6 mu. I have done this for many years, and I do not like making big changes unless I see it work nearby first. On my land with well irrigation, I will put enough fertilizer to hold yield steady, because losing grain costs more than wasting a little fertilizer. For winter wheat, I will use an improved variety, put more nitrogen on wheat because it needs a strong stand before winter and a good push in spring, and I will water about 3 times if the year is normal: once after sowing if the soil is dry, once at jointing, and once around filling. For summer maize, I will use hybrid seed like most people around here, keep fertilizer a little lower than wheat but still not light, and water 2 times if rain is not enough, mainly at big flare stage and grain filling. I farm only 6 mu and mostly by myself, so I will keep the work simple: rotary tillage before wheat, then no-tillage or very light direct seeding for maize after wheat harvest if I can save labor and catch the season. I will spray 2 times on each crop in a normal year, more only if insects or disease come hard. My goal is steady yield, not fancy management.
